items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: The main argument for maintaining our overweight stance on stocks comes down to corporate profitability.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: That means maintaining an overweight position in technology stocks.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: The AI-driven capex boom, and the need for infrastructure to support it, should support the outlook for industrials, another sector on which we have an overweight stance.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Although the sector retains defensive characteristics, higher long-term yields mean utilities’ status as a bond proxy and their reliable dividend payments are less attractive.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: We therefore downgrade utilities to neutral.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Regionally, our preference is for emerging-market stocks (excluding China), which continue to benefit from strong global trade flows, elevated commodity prices, favourable growth dynamics, and extensive exposure to the AI theme.

items.label: Monthly CIO Update, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain positive on equities, with a preference for emerging-market stocks, especially in Asia, where exposure to AI investment is a positive, in our view.

items.label: Monthly CIO Update, Sep 2026
items.text: This is one of the reasons why we’ve upgraded gold to overweight.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We stay constructive on risk but are increasingly selective, favoring AI bottlenecks, shorter-term bonds and opportunities beyond asset class labels.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We stay overweight U.S. equities and upgrade emerging market stocks to overweight but stay focused on opportunities driven by bottlenecks.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: The bond yield outlook and renewed momentum in the AI theme are supportive of our Overweight view on US and Asia ex-Japan equities.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We reinstate our Overweight stance on gold as USD weakness resumes.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Continue to favour corporate and EM bonds over G3 government bonds.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Financial sector an attractive route to broadening exposure.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Fiscal expansion is lifting domestic demand and benefiting the industrial sector, while higher-for-longer rates favour the banking sector.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain Underweight real estate and consumer staples amid weak sentiment and low visibility on the housing recovery.
